Where available, they are available and the documents have been handed over, the translations of such documents have been handed over to the Defence. Other translations are not available. In respect to the translation of Defence documents, the Prosecution acknowledges that there is a challenge for the Defence. The Prosecution has always assisted the Defence far beyond its obligation under the Rules in order to get their case prepared. The Prosecution for the Defence, a certain section within the Prosecution of the Defence has checked to what extent the documents the Defence team wishes to have translated into English are already translated by the Prosecution. A review has revealed that only 5 per cent of the Defence documents are available in English translation. By the way, such translations are actually available and can be handed over at the earliest opportunity, probably tomorrow morning. There is, however, the situation that Defence is facing a challenge all other Defence teams have faced in the past in other proceedings. The other Defence teams have overcome the challenges, and the Prosecution can't see any reason why it should be different in this particular case. In respect to the issue as to whether the Prosecution would be able to provide the Defence team with additional staff for translations, there is a policy decision by the Prosecutor that the Prosecution will not do so. The very last issue I wish to address is the videotape containing portions in Arabic language. The Prosecution is prepared to translate such portions into English. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I thank you very much. So it follows that from the point of view we just heard, that translation is a genuine, real problem, but it is a standing problem, and practical solutions are to be sought by both parties at this stage. I note that both parties are ready and willing to make every effort to have these proceedings take place in the best possible conditions. And when translation problems arise, it will be up to the Trial Chamber to respond to them as they see fit. And as far as B/C/S documents are concerned, in future proceedings we have the possibility of using interpreters to do a vista translations if these documents are produced by either party during examination-in-chief or cross-examination, thanks to the technical facilities we have, these documents could be translated a vista during the hearing. And as I indicated a moment ago, we are going to take it up with the Registry to see to what extent it is possible to add to the resources of the Defence by increasing the hours of the currently available interpreter from 75 upwards. That would enable the Defence to have -- to receive appropriate answers to their requests. And I'm now coming to item -- that was item 9, translation problems. Item 10. Are there other questions that either party would like to raise? If that is the case, would the Defence like to say anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the beginning of today's conference, I informed the Prosecution that today on a web page containing daily newspapers from Bosnia and Herzegovina, we read a report that SFOR soldiers searched the Cantonal Court and the Prosecutor's office in Zenica and removed certain materials. Since this is the Cantonal Court and the Prosecutor's office which are concerned in our case as well and they have been designated as important institutions in the Prosecutor's pre-trial brief, I have asked the Prosecutor to notify today in your presence whether this entry of SFOR into the Cantonal Court in Zenica has anything to do with our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this matter, does Prosecution wish to respond? The floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm prepared to repeat what we already informed the Defence counsel about. This information was as surprising for us as it has been for the Defence. It has certainly not been this particular Prosecution team that has initiated this. This particular Prosecution team is not aware of the SFOR operation that took place today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution has responded to the question you raised.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We are satisfied with the answer. An answer to the contrary would have called for a certain reaction on the part of the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As all the items of the agenda have been covered, I want to conclude by saying that we shall meet again on the 28th November, I believe at 9.00, for the Pre-Trial Conference under our Rule 113 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. In the meantime, I understood, having heard that motions have been filed to the Trial Chamber and the Trial Chamber will do its best to reply in the shortest possible time. Thank you for the spirit of cooperation you have displayed during this Status Conference, and I thank the interpreters and promise them that next time they will have the normal 15 break. This session is adjourned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: at 5.22 p.m.
